pairs: Non quasi crudelis suscitabo eum:
I will not rouse him, as the cruel would do,
quis enim resistere potest vultui meo?
for who is able to withstand my countenance?
Quis ante dedit mihi,
Who has given to me beforehand,
ut reddam ei?
so that I should repay him?
omnia quæ sub cælo sunt, mea sunt.
All things that are under heaven are mine.
Non parcam ei,
I will not spare him,
et verbis potentibus,
nor his powerful words
et ad deprecandum compositis.
and counterfeit attempts at supplication.
Quis revelabit faciem indumenti ejus?
Who can reveal the beauty of his garment?
et in medium oris ejus quis intrabit?
And who can enter the middle of his mouth?
Portas vultus ejus quis aperiet?
Who can open the doors of his face?
per gyrum dentium ejus formido.
I gave fear to the circle of his teeth.
Corpus illius quasi scuta fusilia,
His body is like shields fused together,
compactum squamis se prementibus.
like dense scales pressed over one another.
Una uni conjungitur,
One is joined to another,
et ne spiraculum quidem incedit per eas.
and not even air can pass between them.
Una alteri adhærebit,
They adhere to one another,
et tenentes se nequaquam separabuntur.
and they hold themselves in place and will not be separated.
Sternutatio ejus splendor ignis,
His sneezing has the brilliance of fire,
et oculi ejus ut palpebræ diluculi.
and his eyes are like the eyelids of the morning.
De ore ejus lampades procedunt,
Lamps proceed from his mouth,
sicut tædæ ignis accensæ.
like torches of fire burning brightly.
De naribus ejus procedit fumus,
Smoke passes out of his nostrils,
sicut ollæ succensæ atque ferventis.
like a pot that is heated and boiling.
Halitus ejus prunas ardere facit,
His breath causes coal to burn,
et flamma de ore ejus egreditur.
and a flame comes forth from his mouth.
In collo ejus morabitur fortitudo,
Strength dwells in his neck,
et faciem ejus præcedit egestas.
and destitution goes before his presence.
Membra carnium ejus cohærentia sibi:
The parts of his body work in harmony together.
mittet contra eum fulmina,
He will send lightning bolts against him,
et ad locum alium non ferentur.
and they will not be carried to another place.
Cor ejus indurabitur tamquam lapis,
His heart will be as hard as a stone
et stringetur quasi malleatoris incus.
and as dense as a blacksmith’s anvil.
Cum sublatus fuerit,
When he will be raised up,
timebunt angeli,
the angels will be afraid, and,
et territi purgabuntur.
because they are terrified, they will purify themselves.
Cum apprehenderit eum gladius,
When a sword catches up with him,
subsistere non poterit,
it will not be able to settle in,
neque hasta,
nor a spear,
neque thorax:
nor a breastplate.
reputabit enim quasi paleas ferrum,
For he will consider iron as if it were chaff,
et quasi lignum putridum æs.
and brass as if it were rotten wood.
Non fugabit eum vir sagittarius:
The archer will not cause him to flee;
in stipulam versi sunt ei lapides fundæ.
the stones of the sling have been turned into stubble for him.
Quasi stipulam æstimabit malleum,
He will treat the hammer as if it were stubble,
et deridebit vibrantem hastam.
and he will ridicule those who brandish the spear.
Sub ipso erunt radii solis,
The beams of the sun will be under him,
et sternet sibi aurum quasi lutum.
and he will dispense gold to them as if it were clay.
Fervescere faciet quasi ollam profundum mare,
He will make the depths of the sea boil like a pot,
et ponet quasi cum unguenta bulliunt.
and he will set it to bubble just as ointments do.
Post eum lucebit semita:
A path will shine after him;
æstimabit abyssum quasi senescentem.
he will esteem the abyss as if it were weakening with age.
Non est super terram potestas quæ comparetur ei,
There is no power on the earth that is being compared to him,
qui factus est ut nullum timeret.
who has been made so that he fears no one.
Omne sublime videt:
He sees every prominent thing;
ipse est rex super universos filios superbiæ.
he is king over all the sons of arrogance.
